units.text: INT. REPOSSESSED PIANO SHOWROOM - NIGHT
Rows of grand pianos under sheets, like ghosts at a recital.
One lamp burns on a bench.
The air smells of lacquer and dust.
DETECTIVE HORTENSE LAFLEUR (50s, trench coat, a limp she hides) circles a closed Steinway.
At the far wall, a heavyset man, CLEM BOUDREAUX (40s, pinstripe shirt, nervous), twists a ring on his finger.
Beside him, a girl in an oversized sweatshirt, WREN (15), picks at the lid of a baby grand.
Mr. Boudreaux.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Detective.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: You recognize that piano?
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: It's a Steinway. I recognize most Steinways.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: It came off a truck in Baton Rouge on the ninth.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Plenty came off trucks on the ninth.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: Not with a body inside.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Wren looks up sharply.
Clem stops twisting the ring.
Wren, honey, go wait in the car.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: I'm not leaving you, Uncle Clem.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Your niece?
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: My niece.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: Hello, Wren. I'm Hortense.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Wren says nothing.
Hortense lifts the sheet and raps on the closed lid.
A hollow thud.
Open it, please.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: It's locked.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: Then unlock it.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: I don't have the key.
units.name: CLEM

units.text: Wren does.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Wren's eyes flick to her uncle.
Clem exhales and shuts his eyes.
It's all right, sweetheart. Nobody's in trouble tonight who doesn't deserve to be.
units.name: DETECTIVE LAFLEUR

units.text: Wren slides a small brass key from her sleeve and walks to the Steinway.
The lock turns with a click that echoes through the whole room.
